title: The Room on the Form
subtitle: Hong Kong maintains documents regarding the sleeping space of foreign domestic workers. Issues like storage places, laundry, and cameras may impact this space.
excerpt: Hong Kong maintains documents regarding the sleeping space of foreign domestic workers. Issues like storage places, laundry, and cameras may impact this space.

content.alt: Rows of windows, air conditioners and external pipes on a brightly painted apartment building in Hong Kong.
content.caption: Apartment windows in Hong Kong, March 15, 2024.

content.text: The accommodation form in Hong Kong allows an employer to declare the sleeping place for the foreign domestic workers. An employer can point to the separate room, a room with children, a separated area, or something else. The June 2024 accommodation form requires providing the flat size and number of inhabitants. The form indicates that flats in Hong Kong are quite small and separated rooms for foreign domestic workers are rather rare. The form does not require any minimal bedroom size. Whatever sleeping place is declared, it has to be appropriate and provide reasonable privacy.

Foreign domestic workers usually have to live at the address of the employer. The private agreement between an employer and a foreign domestic worker is generally not enough to allow living somewhere else. Accommodation is a part of the job and future employees need to know where they will live.

The 2017 report of the Mission for Migrant Workers, entitled Pictures from the Inside, says that 43% of the surveyed workers did not have their own room. In case of those who had their own room, 33% said that the room was used also for some household purposes including storing items, doing laundry, and ironing.

This data are taken from the survey made among 3,075 Filipino and Indonesian domestic workers in December 2016-January 2017. The researchers also made separate focus groups. This data cannot establish the living conditions of all Hong Kong foreign domestic workers as of January 2025. Having a room did not mean using it exclusively: household items and laundry gave other people reasons to enter the sleeping place. The number of rooms does not show these other uses.

According to the Labour Department's 2019 employer's guide, while considering hiring a foreign domestic worker, families need to consider accommodation appropriateness and create a place for personal belongings. At the same time, families need to evaluate if some household procedures can intrude on the worker's privacy, for example, other household members coming to the sleeping place for laundry or storing goods.

The housing form indicates that makeshift corridor beds with low privacy and rooms shared with adults or teens of the opposite sex are not appropriate. The essential facilities to be provided for free include bed with bedding, wardrobe, water, lighting, and access to the bathroom. Significant changes in the household, accommodation, or duties require updating accommodation schedule signed by both parties. An employer has to inform the worker about the change and provide the updated schedule copy to the Immigration Department.

It is important where to put the bed when installing the camera in the household. The camera can record the sleeping space together with the whole room. According to the Labour Department's 2023 handbook, there are guidelines for surveillance: an employer should inform the worker about surveillance before its beginning and should not record activities in bathrooms or in the private space of the worker used for rest after work.
